title: Attestation Ledger & Approval UX — PRD ideation
summary: Exploratory PRD focused on an "attestation ledger" UX and approval experience for customer-managed networking changes. Goal is to combine cryptographic evidence bundles with a human-centered approval flow so operators and security reviewers can quickly validate, approve, or reject VPC / edge-network changes while preserving a tamper-evident audit trail.
background: Customers running Redwood Private ask for stronger, auditable proof of network change approvals and a simpler operator workflow. Existing private deployment notes and prototypes emphasize logs and evidence retention, but operators report difficulty reconciling technical proofs with day-to-day approvals. This doc sketches an experience that binds machine-verifiable receipts to human approval steps and surfaces them in a compact, queryable ledger.
goals: 1) Define an attestation ledger model that aggregates operator actions, customer-supplied network evidence (e.g., firewall rules, BGP diff), and cryptographic receipts; 2) Propose a lightweight approval UX where approvers can see concise risk signals and drill into verifiable evidence; 3) Specify audit log schema and retention/exports for compliance (SOX/GDPR/ISO); 4) Define API contracts for integrating ledger proofs with customer SIEMs and internal incident tooling.
non_goals: 1) Replacing full-fledged ticketing systems (we will link to them) — we are not building a Jira competitor; 2) Full HSM design for customers — we will surface KMS/HSM integration points but not implement HSM drivers here; 3) Detailed operator training material — separate deliverable.
user_stories: As a SOC reviewer, I want to see a one-line risk summary for each VPC change with attached cryptographic proof so I can approve or escalate within 5 minutes.
As a Network Operator, I want the system to automatically collect diffs and bind them to the approval event so I don't have to manually attach files.
As a Compliance Auditor, I want tamper-evident export bundles that include event hashes, signer metadata, and a verifiable chain of custody.
As a Customer Admin, I want the ability to require multi-person approvals for high-risk changes and have the ledger enforce approval gates.
As a SRE, I want rollback playbooks surfaced with each approval so I can quickly revert if a change causes regressions.
requirements: REQ-1: Ledger entries must include: change-id, initiator-id, timestamp (ISO8601), human-readable summary, machine-diff payload (base64 compressed), signer list, cryptographic signature(s) (RFC7515-like), and retention-class tag.
REQ-2: Approval gates policy language supporting: single-approver, dual-approver, role-based approvers, and automated timeouts with escalation rules.
REQ-3: UX shows "risk highlights" computed from a ruleset (eg. public-ip exposure, egress to blacklisted CIDRs, port-open to 0.0.0.0/0) with links to raw diffs.
REQ-4: Export API that returns a signed evidence bundle (zip) with manifest.json and a detached signature for customer archival and SIEM ingestion.
REQ-5: Integrations: optional webhook to customer approval systems, syslog export, and S3-compatible retention buckets with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS).
REQ-6: Retention controls exposed per-customer with presets: 90d, 1y, 7y; immutable flag for legal-hold cases.
REQ-7: Immutable audit view for auditors with read-only filters, timeline playhead, and ability to validate signatures via public key material endpoint.
audit_schema: Schema v0.2 (proposal): fields = [change_id, parent_change_id, initiator {id,email,org}, approvers [ {id,email,role,timestamp,decision,signature} ], resources_affected [{type,identifier,pre_state,post_state,diff_sha256}], evidence_blobs [{name,content_type,storage_pointer,sha256}], signatures [{sig_id,signer_pubkey,algorithm,signature_b64}], policy_version, retention_class, created_at, last_modified_at]. All blobs hashed with SHA-256 and recorded in manifest. Manifest signed by orchestrator key and optionally by customer KMS-wrapped key for customer-managed attestations.
ux_flow: 1) Operator submits network change (upload or link). 2) System auto-extracts diffs and flags high-risk signals. 3) Approval modal displays 3-line summary, risk badges, and two primary actions: Approve / Request Changes. 4) If 'Approve', UX prompts for approver role (if required) and collects an optional rationale, then signs locally (if customer-managed key available) or via Redwood signing key and appends signature to ledger. 5) Post-approval page shows 'evidence capsule' with checksum and a direct link to 'Export signed bundle'. 6) For denied changes, UX allows reviewer to create a rollback playbook task linked to the change. Emphasis on minimal clicks for repeat approvals and obvious escalation path.
api_contracts:
- POST /v1/private/changes : submit a change (multipart: metadata + diffs) -> returns change_id
- GET /v1/private/changes/{id} : returns ledger entry + signed manifest link
- POST /v1/private/changes/{id}/approve : {approver_id,decision,rationale,signature_b64(optional)} -> returns updated ledger entry
- GET /v1/private/changes/{id}/export?format=evidence_zip : returns pre-signed download
- GET /v1/private/keys/public : returns current verifier keys and key rotation history
Auth: mTLS for Private, token-based for Dedicated/Hosted. Webhooks: on_approve/on_reject payloads mirror ledger event schema.
security_and_compliance:
- KMS integration points: allow customers to bring their own KMS keys to sign proofs. If BYOK used, signing operation is proxied and no raw key material is stored by Redwood.
- HSM: surface parameter to require HSM-backed signing for any approver who opts in; implementation deferred to infra team.
- Tamper evidence: chain-of-hashes + detached signatures + key transparency endpoint for verification.
- Data residency: retention and storage region selectable per-customer; exports include proof of region and storage class.
- Privacy: redact PII in public summaries, keep full initiator metadata in auditor-only view.
- Compliance: provide preset manifests that satisfy ISO 27001 / SOC2 / GDPR audit requests (template mapping to each control).
metrics_and_slo: Primary metrics: approval_latency_median (target < 10 min for low-risk), approval_latency_p95 (< 48hr for high-risk with auto-escalation), signature_validation_fail_rate (target <0.1%), export_generation_time_median (< 5s for small bundles), audit_query_time_p95 (<2s). SLOs: 99.9% availability of ledger read APIs, 99.5% for write/approve APIs for Dedicated customers. Sampling: for Hosted, sample 10% of approvals to keep short-term, ephemeral proofs for debugging; customers can opt into full retention.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Create + append + read operations can be performed via API and reflected in UI; evidence bundle validates with public keys endpoint.
AC-2: End-to-end signing path works with Redwood keys and with a simulated customer-managed KMS (mock), including key rotation handling.
AC-3: UX shows risk badges computed from diffs and clicking into raw diffs displays unified diff text; performance within UX latency budget (<300ms for badge compute on typical diff sizes).
AC-4: Export API returns a signed zip; auditor can validate signature using provided public key and manifest.
AC-5: Retention policy honored: entries marked immutable cannot be deleted via API and show legal-hold flag in UI.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (alpha): internal only for private-deployments pilot customers — manual onboarding, feature-flagged. Phase 1 (beta): add KMS BYOK support, webhook integrations, and UI polishing; invite 5 customers. Phase 2 (GA): retention presets, region routing, and compliance templates; enable self-serve in console for Dedicated and Private customers. Phase 3: marketplace connectors for SIEM and ticketing exporters.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customer confusion around what a "signed" approval means. Mitigation: inline help, examples of bundle validation, and short video walkthroughs.
Risk: KMS integration complexity across cloud vendors. Mitigation: start with AWS KMS and GCP KMS adapters, provide documented shim for on-prem HSMs.
Risk: Large diffs causing export latency. Mitigation: chunked uploads, resumable export generation, and progress indicators in UI.
Risk: Legal requests to alter ledger. Mitigation: immutable flags + legal-hold workflow + export-of-records with custody chain.
notes_and_next_steps:
- Run a 2-week discovery with 2 pilot customers (legal + ops) to validate evidence bundle expectations.
- Prototype a lightweight web UI mock for approval flow and run moderated usability sessions.
- Coordinate with infra (Ravi) for KMS/HSM requirements and with SRE (Janine) for ledger availability targets.
- Create a small engineering spike to implement manifest signing and public key endpoint.
